source: TMUA 2017 · Paper 2 · Question 11 · Official worked answer

hints.title: Check that these areas are signed integrals too
hints.body: f is increasing and f(0)=0, so f(x)≥0 for positive x. In particular, the graph is above or on the axis from a to b.
hints.recap: Geometric area equals the integral on an interval where the function is nonnegative.
hints.pitfall: Increasing alone would not ensure a positive graph without the given reference value.
hints.pause: Check that g is also nonnegative on this interval.

recall.reminder: Check the sign before identifying an integral with area.

hints.title: Recognise a constant vertical shift
hints.body: b is fixed, so f(b) is a number. Adding 2f(b) raises every point of the graph by the same height.
hints.recap: A function value at a fixed input is a constant in x.
hints.pitfall: This is f(b), not the varying function f(x).
hints.pause: Sketch the extra strip between the two graphs from a to b.

recall.reminder: Separate constant output translations from changes to the input.

hints.title: Integrate the added constant
hints.body: The difference between the two functions is constant with respect to x. Integrate that difference over the stated interval and add it to the original integral.
hints.recap: An integral of a constant includes the interval length.
hints.pitfall: Do not confuse the fixed number f(b) with the variable function f(x).
hints.pause: Calculate the extra area and express the total in the given quantities.

recall.reminder: An integral of a constant includes the interval length.

solution:
Both functions are nonnegative on [a,b]. The vertical shift from f to g is the constant 2f(b), so the extra area is a rectangle of width b−a and height 2f(b).

The total area is R+2(b−a)f(b). Answer B.
knowledgePattern: Add a rectangle under a vertically translated increasing function
